ON (default): prices are read live from the world economy, including markets you have not visited. OFF: only prices you have seen in person are used.
Observed prices older than this are ignored. 0 = never expire.
Never scan, suggest or auto-trade with settlements at war with you.
Limit price scans to markets within this straight-line distance. 0 = whole map.
Best-buy hints require at least this many units in stock. 0 = off. Live-price mode only, because observed mode records prices, not stock levels.
Markets farther than this many travel days are hidden from tooltips, and no suggested route's total trip (you -> buy town -> sell town) may exceed it. Default 3.
A separate, stricter travel ceiling for villages. Default 1.

Apply the resale safety factor to the sell side when ranking and totalling routes, so listed profit allows for prices drifting before you arrive. OFF shows raw margins. Routes must clear the safety factor to be listed either way, since that is the same test quick-buy applies on arrival.

Price a lot unit by unit through the game's own price model, so quantity and profit account for your own buying moving the price. OFF prices every unit at the first unit's price, which reads higher than the trip will pay. Towns and live-price mode only: villages expose no supply or demand data, and observed mode does not read live market internals.

Order the panel by profit per day, discounted by how likely that profit is to survive the trip. The discount accounts for margin left after the bulk walk, stock depth, trip length, caravan traffic, and in observed mode the age of the prices. OFF ranks on raw profit per day and the Score column shows that instead.
Adds the best known buy and sell markets, with stock and travel time, to item tooltips.
Skips the vanilla merchandise rumor block so the tooltip shows one consistent set of price hints.
Colors trade-good and livestock rows in the inventory by how this market's price compares with the best known market.

Key that opens the ledger panel on the campaign map. A single key name such as T, Y or F5, optionally with Ctrl, Alt or Shift in front, e.g. "Ctrl+T". This mod does not take keys away from the game, so a bare key the game also uses will trigger both actions. Use a modifier to avoid that.
A clickable TradeLord button on the right edge of the campaign map that opens the ledger panel. Turn OFF if it interferes with map clicks.
Shows the quick-sell entry in town and village menus. It also controls the quick-trade entry, which sells before it buys; with this off, neither appears.
Sells policy-approved goods automatically when you enter a market. Trade XP is awarded.
Buys profitable goods automatically when you enter a market, after any auto-sell. Turning this on also enables quick-buy.

Full automation. Reads as ON exactly when both toggles above are ON, and switches them together. Selling runs first, so profit and Trade XP are awarded before any buying. With this ON the separate quick-sell and quick-buy menu entries are hidden; quick-trade remains for manual re-runs.

The margin every trade must clear, in both directions. Sell only if the price exceeds your cost basis by at least this much. Buy, or list a route, only if the far market exceeds the local price by this much after the resale safety factor. Raising it trades less.
Hold back this many days of food before selling any. The cheapest food per day fed is reserved first, and livestock only if nothing else covers the reserve. 0 sells every scrap of food.
What automated trading may do with food. The days-of-supply reserve above is separate and still applies.
What automated trading may do with charcoal, hardwood, iron ore and ingots. Set 0 to keep smithing stock out of automated trading entirely.

What automated trading may do with sheep, cattle and hogs. Buying is capped by the game's own herding calculation, so it will not push the party into the herd speed penalty. Mounts and pack animals are never bought or sold by policy and this setting does not affect them; only an explicit always-sell entry can move one.
Never auto-trade unique or player-crafted items. Mounts and pack animals are protected by policy regardless of this setting; only an explicit always-sell entry can move those.
Locked items in the inventory screen are never auto-traded. Locks are matched as the game stores them, by item and modifier.

How profit is measured, and so how much Trade XP a sale earns. 0: average of what you paid. 1: last price you paid. 2: cheapest known buy price. Goods you never bought have no price you paid, so every mode values those at the cheapest market you know of; selling one below that earns no profit and no Trade XP.
Also quick-sell weapons and armor of this tier and below. Locks and protections still apply.

Skip selling here when this market pays clearly less than the best known market. Goods you never bought have no cost basis, so the floor always applies to those; this setting controls whether it also applies to goods you bought, which the profit margin already covers.
With the above ON: sell here anyway if this market pays at least this fraction of the best known price.

Goods quick-sell must never sell, by item id. An item id is the short internal name of a good, such as grain, wine or iron_ore. TradeLord.log names the id of every good it moves, so trade once and read the ids off the log. Quick-buy leaves these alone too, since it would have no way to sell them on.

Goods quick-sell always sells, by item id, past the category policies, the unique and crafted protection and the food reserve. The never-sell list above and an inventory lock still hold. This is the only way to sell a mount or a pack animal.
Buy goods here that sell for more elsewhere, within the caps below. Only goods actually in stock are bought.
Never spend below this much gold. Default 300, which is enough to barter your way out of two hostile encounters and still meet a wage payment after a shopping trip.
Most units of one item quick-buy takes per visit. Default 32.
Also cap spending per item per visit in denars.
Total denars quick-buy may spend per settlement visit. Default 1000.
Assume only this fraction of the best sell price is still available by the time you arrive.
Grain is heavy and low margin, so buying it fills the cargo for little return. Selling and the food reserve are unaffected. ON by default.
Items quick-buy must never purchase. Selling them is unaffected.
Quick-sell/quick-buy also in village menus; villages join the price scans.

Report what quick-sell and quick-buy would do, without trading. Treat the result as a best case: nothing moves, so the market does not react and every unit is priced at today's opening price. A real pass stops at the unit where the margin runs out, so it usually trades less and gets less per unit. The merchant's gold, your carry weight, the gold reserve and every per-item and per-visit cap are modelled exactly; only your own effect on the price is not.
No TradeLord trading before this campaign day, from the menu or on entry. Prices in a new campaign have not settled yet.
Scales the Trade XP awarded for automated profit. 0 disables XP.

Moves a map tracker to whichever nearby town pays most for your current cargo. Re-evaluated daily and whenever you enter or leave a settlement, so it follows what you are carrying now. Limited by the travel ceiling below. ON by default; clicking a town in the ledger panel still pins a marker by hand.
The auto-marker ignores towns farther than this many travel days away. Default 1.5.
Play a coin sound when a quick-sell or quick-buy pass actually moves something. A pass that trades nothing stays silent.
Name the goods in the one-line trade summary, e.g. 'TradeLord sold 8 Olives, 3 Wine for 240 denars', instead of a bare item count. The full list is always written to TradeLord.log.
